title: CERTIFICATE ROTATION
body: InfoSec requires certificate rotation across all services by Friday. InfoSec has known about this expiry for eight months. You learned about it in this sentence. The announcement thanks teams in advance for their partnership, which is what it is called when one party does the work and the other party does the announcing.

title: MANDATORY FRAMEWORK MIGRATION
body: The Standards Body has ratified Framework Nine as the enterprise standard. All services must migrate within two weeks. Framework Nine was chosen for its stability, by a committee that has not deployed software since Framework Four, which they also chose, which is what you are migrating off of.

title: ANNUAL ATTESTATION CAMPAIGN
body: The annual attestation campaign is live. Every party member must certify adherence to the Acceptable Use Policy, the Data Handling Policy, and the Policy on Policies, by Wednesday. The campaign was planned for a full year. The window for completing it is five days. This ratio is not discussed.

title: VENDOR SECURITY QUESTIONNAIRE
body: A 247-question security questionnaire is due for a tool your party has run in production for three years. Question 12 asks whether the tool is currently in use. Question 118 asks what would happen if it were. Answering honestly triggers a review. Answering dishonestly is a policy violation. Not answering is Friday's problem, and today is Wednesday.

title: RETROACTIVE ARCHITECTURE REVIEW
body: The Architecture Review Board requests a review of the architecture you shipped last quarter. The review is forward-looking, the Board explains, in that its findings will apply to you going forward. Materials are due in ten days, in the Board's template, which requires diagrams in a notation the Board is currently revising.

title: STATUS TEMPLATE VERSION 7
body: The PMO has released Status Template v7 and requires all programs to restate their current and historical status in the new format by Thursday. Version 7 differs from version 6 in the order of two columns. The restatement of history is required so that the record is consistent, which is a thing history has never been and a spreadsheet must be.

title: QUARTERLY ACCESS RECERTIFICATION
body: All access grants must be recertified within six days. Anything unreviewed will be revoked automatically, for safety. The recertification tool lists 400 grants per member, of which roughly twelve are recognisable, and offers a Select All button that the training video, mandatory, twenty minutes, specifically forbids you to use.

title: STRUCTURED LOGGING STANDARD v2
body: All services must emit logs in the new structured format by month end. The standard is 80 pages. The reference implementation is a code snippet in an appendix, marked illustrative, that does not compile. Teams that adopted v1 early are furthest from compliance, a sentence the Standards Body has read and approved.

title: DISASTER RECOVERY EXERCISE
body: A mandatory disaster recovery exercise is scheduled for release week. Participation demonstrates resilience. The exercise simulates the loss of a region. Your party will simulate continuing to function. The scheduling of the exercise during release week was itself a small disaster, from which there is no recovery exercise.

title: RESOURCE TAGGING MANDATE
body: Every cloud resource must carry a cost-center tag by Friday, at which point untagged resources will be deleted by an automated governance process. The mandate's FAQ addresses the question of what happens to untagged production resources with the phrase: see above. Above is the sentence about deletion.

title: API CATALOG REGISTRATION
body: All APIs must be registered in the Enterprise API Catalog within nine days, including schema, owner, and lifecycle stage. The catalog is itself an API. It is not registered in itself. This was raised at the Board and minuted as out of scope, a phrase the Board can apply to anything except your deadline.

title: OPEN SOURCE LICENSE ATTESTATION
body: Legal requires an attestation of every dependency license in your tree, including transitive dependencies, by the twelfth. Your tree has 1,400 nodes. The attestation portal accepts entries one at a time and logs out after ten minutes of what it calls inactivity, by which it means data entry.

title: IDENTITY PROVIDER CUTOVER
body: The identity provider migrates Saturday night. All service integrations must be re-authenticated before the cutover or after it, but not during it, and the window for before closes Friday, and the announcement is dated today, and today is Tuesday. A support channel exists. It is staffed until Friday, close of business, in a timezone that is not yours.

title: DATA CLASSIFICATION SWEEP
body: Every data store must be classified into one of four sensitivity tiers within ten days, using a form that offers three. The guidance document resolves this by defining tier four as tier three with additional considerations. The considerations are not enumerated. Classification is binding once submitted and cannot be revised without a reclassification review, which uses the same form.

title: CRITICAL VULNERABILITY SLA
body: A critical vulnerability requires remediation within 30 days of disclosure. Disclosure was 22 days ago; the notice reached you today. The remediation must be deployed through a change window, and the next change window opens in 15 days. Teams are encouraged to be proactive. The encouragement is the only part with no deadline.

title: MANDATORY SECURE DEVELOPMENT TRAINING
body: Six hours of secure development training are due by Friday for all party members, including the Security Champion, who wrote the module the training is based on and must now watch a narrator read it to her slowly. The training portal is down for maintenance until Thursday. The deadline is unaffected, the portal team confirms, from inside the portal.
